questions.stem: Refraction of light at the boundary between two media occurs because the light changes its

options.text: speed
frequency
colour
amplitude

questions.explanation: Light travels at different speeds in different transparent media. When a wavefront crosses the boundary obliquely, one edge slows down before the other, which swings the whole wavefront round and changes the direction of travel. The frequency is fixed by the source and does not change on refraction.

distractorRationale.b: Frequency is set by the source and is unchanged by refraction; it is the wavelength that changes along with the speed
distractorRationale.c: Colour is determined by frequency, so it does not change. Different colours are refracted by different amounts, but that is a consequence of refraction, not its cause
distractorRationale.d: Amplitude relates to brightness and is not what makes the ray bend

questions.stem: Light travels faster in water than in air.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Water is optically denser than air, with a refractive index of about 1.33 compared with 1.00 for air. Since n = c/v, a larger n means a smaller speed: light travels at about 2.3 × 10⁸ m/s in water against 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in air. That slowing down is exactly why a ray bends towards the normal on entering water.

distractorRationale.a: Light is slowest in the optically densest medium. If light were faster in water, rays entering water would bend away from the normal, which is the opposite of what is observed

questions.stem: The refractive index of a glass block is 1.50 and the speed of light in vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Calculate the speed of light in the glass. Give your answer in metres per second.
questions.explanation: Using $n = \frac{c}{v}$, we get $v = \frac{c}{n} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^{8}}{1.50} = 2.0 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m/s}$. Multiplying instead of dividing would give 4.5 × 10⁸ m/s, which is faster than light in vacuum and therefore impossible.

questions.stem: A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The angle of incidence is 45° and the angle of refraction is 30°. Calculate the refractive index of the liquid.
questions.explanation: By Snell's law, $n = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \frac{\sin 45^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{0.707}{0.500} = 1.41$. Refractive index is a ratio, so it carries no unit, and the value is greater than 1 as expected for a real medium.

questions.stem: A ray of light travelling in air strikes a glass surface at an angle of incidence of 30°. If the refractive index of the glass is 1.50, calculate the angle of refraction. Give your answer in degrees.
questions.explanation: From Snell's law, $\sin r = \frac{\sin i}{n} = \frac{\sin 30^\circ}{1.50} = \frac{0.500}{1.50} = 0.333$, so $r = \sin^{-1}(0.333) = 19.5^\circ$. The ray entered a denser medium, so the angle of refraction is correctly smaller than the angle of incidence.

questions.stem: Calculate the critical angle for light travelling from glass of refractive index 1.50 into air. Give your answer in degrees.
questions.explanation: At the critical angle the refracted ray grazes the surface with r = 90°, so Snell's law reduces to $\sin C = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{1.50} = 0.667$. Hence $C = \sin^{-1}(0.667) = 41.8^\circ$. Any ray inside the glass meeting the surface at more than this angle is totally internally reflected.

questions.stem: Total internal reflection can occur only when light travels

options.text: from a less dense to a denser medium at any angle
from a denser to a less dense medium at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle
from a denser to a less dense medium along the normal
from a less dense to a denser medium at an angle smaller than the critical angle

questions.explanation: Two conditions must be met together. The light must be going from the optically denser medium towards the less dense one, and the angle of incidence in the denser medium must exceed the critical angle. Only then does no refracted ray escape and the whole beam reflect back inside.

distractorRationale.a: Going into a denser medium the ray bends towards the normal and always refracts, so total internal reflection is impossible in that direction
distractorRationale.c: A ray along the normal passes straight out without bending, so it is not reflected back
distractorRationale.d: This has both conditions wrong: the wrong direction and the wrong inequality

questions.stem: A pond is 1.2 m deep. If the refractive index of water is 4/3, calculate the apparent depth of the pond when viewed from directly above. Give your answer in metres.
questions.explanation: Since $n = \frac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}}$, apparent depth $= \frac{\text{real depth}}{n} = \frac{1.2}{4/3} = 1.2 \times \frac{3}{4} = 0.90\ \text{m}$. The bottom appears raised by 1.2 − 0.90 = 0.30 m, which is why water always looks shallower than it is.

questions.stem: A coin lying at the bottom of a beaker of water appears to be 3.0 cm below the water surface when viewed from directly above. If the refractive index of water is 4/3, calculate the real depth of the water. Give your answer in centimetres.
questions.explanation: Rearranging $n = \frac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}}$ gives real depth $= n \times$ apparent depth $= \frac{4}{3} \times 3.0 = 4.0\ \text{cm}$. This question runs the calculation in reverse, so here you multiply by n instead of dividing; the real depth must come out larger than the apparent depth, and 4.0 cm > 3.0 cm confirms it.

questions.stem: The refractive indices of water, glass and diamond are 1.33, 1.50 and 2.42 respectively. Which of these media has the smallest critical angle when bounded by air?

options.text: Water
Glass
Diamond
All three have the same critical angle

questions.explanation: Since sin C = 1/n, a larger refractive index gives a smaller value of sin C and therefore a smaller critical angle. Diamond has the largest n, so it has the smallest C: sin C = 1/2.42 = 0.413, giving C = 24.4°, against 41.8° for glass and 48.8° for water. This very small critical angle traps light inside a cut diamond through many internal reflections, producing its brilliance.

distractorRationale.a: Water has the smallest refractive index of the three, so it has the largest critical angle at about 48.8°
distractorRationale.b: Glass sits in the middle at about 41.8°
distractorRationale.d: Critical angle depends directly on refractive index, and the three indices are all different

questions.stem: According to Snell's law, what is the relationship between the angle of incidence and the angle of refraction?

options.text: sin(i)/sin(r) = n
n = sin(i) + sin(r)
sin(i) = sin(r) * n
n = sin(r)/sin(i)

questions.explanation: Snell's law states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is constant and equal to the refractive index (n) of the two media. This relationship helps in understanding how light bends when it passes from one medium to another.

distractorRationale.b: This option incorrectly suggests addition instead of a ratio.
distractorRationale.c: This option misrepresents the relationship by equating sin(i) directly to sin(r) multiplied by n.
distractorRationale.d: This option incorrectly suggests that the refractive index is the ratio of sin(r) to sin(i), which is not in line with Snell's law.
